definition: Backup speed: Incremental > Differential > Full. Restore speed: Full > Differential > Incremental. Storage per backup: Incremental < Differential < Full. Restore complexity: Full (1 set) < Differential (2 sets) < Incremental (full + all incrementals).

EU regulation governing personal data of EU residents — applies to any organization worldwide that handles EU residents' data. Key rights: right to access, right to erasure ("right to be forgotten"), right to data portability. Requires: consent for data collection, breach notification within 72 hours, data minimization. Penalties up to €20M or 4% of global annual revenue.

AI systems that create new content — text, images, code, audio, video — based on patterns learned from training data. Responds to prompts to generate novel output. Distinguished from discriminative AI (which classifies/analyzes existing content). Examples: large language models (text generation), image generators (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E), code assistants (Copilot).
Multi-touch trackpad: pinch to zoom, two-finger scroll, three-finger swipe for Mission Control/app switching, four-finger pinch for Launchpad.

Tape/backup rotation scheme: Son = daily backups (kept for one week). Father = weekly backups (kept for one month). Grandfather = monthly backups (kept for one year or longer). Provides granular recent recovery points plus long-term archival. Classic scheme for tape-based backup environments.
Syncs from on-premises AD or LDAP to Google Workspace. ONE-WAY sync only (on-prem to cloud). Runs on a schedule. Syncs users, groups, OUs, contacts.
Stream mode: files in cloud, download on demand. Mirror mode: all files synced locally. Shared drives: team-accessible storage separate from individual accounts.

Google's cloud productivity suite. Gmail (IMAP/SMTP), Google Drive, Docs/Sheets/Slides (real-time collaboration), Google Meet (video), Google Chat (messaging), Google Sites. Storage shared between Gmail and Drive.

Passive receive-only — GPS receiver decodes signals from satellites, no data is transmitted from device. Requires 4+ satellites for accurate 3D positioning. Limitations: blocked by buildings, dense foliage, tunnels (urban canyon effect). Time to First Fix (TTFF): cold start (no almanac) can take 30–60 seconds. Assisted GPS (A-GPS): uses cellular/Wi-Fi data to download almanac faster — dramatically reduces TTFF.

Up to 128 partitions — all primary, no extended/logical distinction needed. Protective MBR prevents MBR-only tools from damaging GPT disk. Partition table backed up at end of disk. Required for drives over 2 TB. Required for UEFI boot.

MBR (Master Boot Record): partition table in first 512-byte sector. Max 4 primary partitions (or 3 primary + 1 extended with logical partitions inside). Max drive size: 2 TB. Works with legacy BIOS firmware. MBR + BIOS = legacy pair. GPT (GUID Partition Table): stores partition info in multiple locations (redundant). Up to 128 partitions. No practical size limit — handles drives larger than 2 TB. Requires UEFI firmware. GPT + UEFI = modern pair. Windows 11 requires GPT + UEFI.

Most consumer GPUs use integrated dual or triple fan cooler with heat pipes. Blower-style cooler: single fan, exhausts hot air directly out PCIe slot bracket — preferred in multi-GPU or poor-airflow cases. Open-air (standard): recirculates some heat into case — requires good case airflow. Waterblock: custom liquid cooling for GPU — maximum performance, requires custom loop.

GPU driver crash: screen goes black briefly, then recovers ("Display driver stopped responding and recovered"). Frequent crashes: GPU overheating, corrupted driver, VRAM fault. Fix: DDU clean uninstall, reinstall latest driver. GPU not detected: check PCIe slot seating, check 6+2 pin power connectors plugged in.

Digitizer input device for drawing/design. Stylus with pressure sensitivity (512–8192 levels). Maps tablet surface to screen. Wacom dominant in professional market. Built-in display variants (Wacom Cintiq): draw directly on screen.

Configures system and user policies on Windows Pro and higher. NOT available on Windows Home. Two sections: Computer Configuration (applies to all users of the machine) and User Configuration (applies to specific user accounts). Covers: password policy, account lockout, audit policy, software restrictions, Windows Update behavior, screensaver settings, and much more. Apply immediately with: gpupdate /force.

Automatically assigns Microsoft 365 licenses based on Azure AD group membership. When user joins a group → receives license. When removed → license revoked. Requires Azure AD Premium. Eliminates manual license management at scale.
Separate SSID + separate VLAN. Internet access only — no internal network access. Different password from main network. Isolates untrusted devices (visitors, IoT).

Do NOT argue, contradict aggressively, or become defensive. Steps: listen without interrupting, acknowledge their frustration (empathize — "I understand this is frustrating"), remain calm and professional, focus on resolving the issue, set realistic expectations for timeline. Never match the customer's emotional state. Escalate if abusive (threats, profanity directed at you).

Physical license enforcement devices (USB security dongles, HASP keys). Must be physically attached for the application to launch. Used in some professional/engineering software. Smart card readers serve similar purpose.

Magnetic storage. Spinning platters read by mechanical read/write heads on actuator arms. 3.5" (desktop), 2.5" (laptop). SATA interface (modern), PATA (legacy). Speeds: 5400 RPM (energy efficient, laptops), 7200 RPM (standard desktop/NAS), 10K–15K RPM (enterprise SCSI/SAS). Sequential read/write fast; random I/O slow due to head seek time. Susceptible to physical shock (especially while operating). Best for: high-capacity storage, bulk archival (low cost per GB).

Clicking or grinding noise: read/write head is physically failing or platter damage — IMMINENT failure. Immediately make a backup copy of all data before the drive dies completely. Very slow file access (seconds for simple operations). CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) errors when copying files — data integrity failure. Frequent application crashes or freezes (reading from bad sectors). SMART alert popup from OS.

Wider brightness and color range. VESA DisplayHDR standards: HDR400 (400 nits peak), HDR600, HDR1000. True HDR requires FALD backlight (full array local dimming) or OLED. Edge-lit monitors with HDR400 = "marketing HDR" — minimal real-world improvement.

USB headset: digital audio, built-in DAC/ADC, no interference. 3.5mm TRS/TRRS: analog, universal. TRRS (4-pole): combined headphone + microphone in one plug. TRS (3-pole): headphone or line-out only. Bluetooth headset: wireless, codecs affect quality (SBC standard, aptX, LDAC high-quality). Noise-canceling microphone: directional mic, background noise reduction — improves call quality.
Files beginning with a dot (.) are hidden. ls -a or ls -la shows hidden files. ~/.bashrc, ~/.ssh/ are common hidden configuration files.

Unexpected network traffic when user is idle — potential command-and-control (C2) communication, data exfiltration, or botnet activity. Monitor with Resource Monitor > Network tab or netstat -ano in CMD. Identify process with suspicious outbound connections.

Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act. Governs PHI privacy and security. Requires: access controls, audit logs of PHI access, encryption, breach notification within 60 days of discovery. Penalties: $100–$50,000 per violation up to $1.9M/year depending on culpability. IT technicians in healthcare must understand HIPAA obligations.
DEPRECATED — removed in Windows 10 version 1803. Replaced by simpler sharing options. If the exam mentions HomeGroup, it is referring to legacy/deprecated functionality.

C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts — plaintext file that maps hostnames to IP addresses, checked before DNS. Malware modifies it to redirect legitimate domains (e.g., bank website) to attacker-controlled IPs. Symptom: legitimate site loads wrong page or shows certificate error. Fix: inspect hosts file in Notepad (as admin), remove malicious entries. Legitimate entries are minimal — localhost and possibly a few corporate entries.

Server racks arranged so all servers face the same direction: cold aisle (front of servers) receives cooled air from CRAC units. Hot aisle (rear of servers) exhausts hot air back to CRAC return. Containment panels seal the tops and ends of aisles to prevent cold and hot air from mixing — dramatically improves cooling efficiency and reduces HVAC load.

Share device's cellular data connection to other devices. Methods: Wi-Fi hotspot (most common — creates a Wi-Fi AP from phone), USB tethering (wired, charges phone simultaneously, often fastest), Bluetooth tethering (slower, more power-efficient than Wi-Fi). Carrier may throttle hotspot data or require add-on plan.

Padlock + https:// = TLS-encrypted, CA-validated connection. Certificate warnings (expired, self-signed, mismatch, revoked) = investigate before proceeding — possible MITM. Never proceed past warning on sensitive sites.

Layer 1 (Physical). Repeater — receives signal on one port, broadcasts to ALL other ports. Creates a single collision domain (all devices share bandwidth and collide). Obsolete — completely replaced by switches. No intelligence — cannot learn MAC addresses. Exam context: understand why hubs are inferior to switches.

Target: 45%–55% relative humidity (some standards allow 40%–60%). Too high humidity: condensation forms on components — causes corrosion, shorts, and failure. Too low humidity: ESD risk increases dramatically (static electricity builds up more easily in dry conditions). Data centers use precision CRAC (Computer Room Air Conditioning) units with humidity control, not standard HVAC.
Software layer that creates, runs, and manages virtual machines by abstracting physical hardware. Allocates physical CPU, RAM, storage, and network resources to VMs. Two types: Type 1 and Type 2.

Removable metal plate that fits into rear of case, with cutouts matching the motherboard's rear port layout. Included with motherboard. Must be installed before mounting motherboard. Provides port labeling and EMI shielding. Grounding fingers contact the motherboard's rear I/O area.
Apple's cloud sync service. Syncs contacts, calendar, photos, documents, and Keychain across Apple devices. iCloud Drive for cloud file storage.

Parallel ATA — older drive interface. 40-pin ribbon cable (80-wire for ATA-100/133 — extra ground wires reduce interference). Wide flat ribbon cable. Master/slave jumper configuration on drive. 133 MB/s maximum. Completely replaced by SATA. Exam context: recognize physically (wide ribbon cable).

Intrusion Detection System (IDS): monitors traffic for attack signatures/anomalies — generates alerts, no automatic blocking. Inline or tap (passive). Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): inline — can block malicious traffic automatically. Signature-based: detects known attacks. Anomaly/behavior-based: detects deviations from baseline. IPS introduces latency (in traffic path). False positive: legitimate traffic flagged as malicious. False negative: malicious traffic not detected.

ifconfig: legacy Linux network config tool (deprecated). ip addr show: displays interface addresses. ip route show: displays routing table. ip link: interface state management. Replaces ifconfig on modern Linux distributions.

A complete snapshot of a configured system (OS + drivers + apps + settings) captured into a single image file using DISM, Sysprep, or third-party tools. Stored on a deployment server. New machines PXE boot to server and pull identical image. Guarantees consistency — no configuration drift. Zero-touch deployment = fully automated from power-on to first login.

Conducted before any change is approved. Asks: what systems depend on what is being changed? Who are the affected users? What is the blast radius if the change goes wrong? How long will any outage last? Informed by CMDB dependency mapping. Allows stakeholders to make an informed approval decision.

Device impact: CPU/RAM/disk consumption affecting overall machine performance. Network impact: cloud-connected apps, update services, collaboration tools can saturate bandwidth — configure metered connections if needed. Operation impact: compatibility conflicts with existing software, security software may flag new apps — test in staging environment first. Business impact: licensing costs, user training, productivity disruption during transition.

Print head of pins strikes inked ribbon against paper. Creates characters from dot patterns. Loud mechanical operation. Multi-part forms (carbonless copy paper): only impact printer can create carbon copies. Still used in: warehouses for packing slips, legal environments requiring carbon copies, point-of-sale systems for receipts requiring carbon.
False identity (vendor, IT contractor, new hire) to gain access or extract info. Props + confident demeanor + plausible pretext. Mitigation: verify identity via secondary channel, not appearance.

Installs new OS version over existing one. Preserves user files, installed applications, and settings. Options during in-place upgrade from USB: (1) Keep everything (files + apps), (2) Keep data only (files, not apps), (3) Clean install. Windows 10 → 11 free upgrade used this mechanism.

Many regulations require breach notification: HIPAA (60 days), GDPR (72 hours), various state laws (30–90 days). IT technicians who discover evidence of a breach or policy violation must follow the incident response and reporting chain — report to supervisor/security team, do not investigate independently, preserve evidence.
Complete combustion — produces ash, no recoverable data. Highest classification levels. Requires controlled facility with chain of custody.

Artifacts (random pixels, geometric shapes, color corruption): usually GPU overheating or VRAM failure — check GPU temperature, clean fans, reapply thermal paste. Run GPU stress test (FurMark) to reproduce and confirm. Driver issue can also cause artifacts — DDU (Display Driver Uninstaller) clean reinstall.

Resolution not matching native panel: right-click desktop > Display settings > resolution (set to recommended/native). Generic driver may not know native resolution. Install correct GPU driver. Scaling issues on HiDPI: set DPI scaling in Display Settings (100%, 125%, 150%).

Copies only data changed since the LAST BACKUP OF ANY TYPE (full or incremental). Archive bit cleared after each incremental. Each incremental is small and fast. Restore requires: last full + ALL incrementals since (potentially many sets). Fastest to back up. Slowest to restore. Highest risk if any incremental in the chain is corrupt.

Very short range, line-of-sight. Traditional use: TV/AV remote controls. IrDA (legacy): device-to-device file transfer (replaced by Bluetooth). Modern use in phones: IR blaster allows phone to control TVs, ACs, and AV equipment. Passive IR (PIR): motion sensing in security systems.
Child objects inherit NTFS permissions from parent by default. Can be broken to set explicit non-inherited permissions on a specific object.

Sprays microscopic droplets of liquid ink from print head onto paper. Thermal inkjet: heats element to vaporize ink, forcing droplet out (HP). Piezoelectric: electric current deforms element to expel droplet (Epson). Cartridges: CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, black). Separate or combined cartridges. Best for: color photos, low-to-medium volume color printing. Negatives: ink expensive per page, heads clog if unused for extended periods, ink can smear if paper/ink mismatch. Head cleaning: wastes ink but clears clogged nozzles.

Streaks, bands, or missing sections in output: clogged print head nozzles — run head cleaning utility from printer software. Multiple cleanings may be needed. If nozzle test pattern shows missing lines = confirmed clogged. Faded output: ink cartridge low or empty. Smearing wet ink: wrong paper type for ink (glossy vs plain), ink not drying fast enough — use correct media type, reduce print speed.
Legitimate access used to cause harm — intentional (theft, sabotage) or unintentional (negligence). Mitigations: least privilege, access reviews, UBA, separation of duties.

Low storage causes: app crashes, inability to download/install updates (both app updates and OS updates), inability to take photos/videos, performance degradation. Remediation: delete unused apps, move media to cloud/SD card, clear app caches, use Settings > Storage > Free Up Space (Android) or Offload Unused Apps (iOS).

Graphics processing built into CPU die. Intel: UHD Graphics (Core series), Iris Xe. AMD: Radeon Graphics (Ryzen APUs with RDNA2). Shares system RAM (VRAM is allocated from main RAM — reduces RAM available to CPU). Sufficient for: everyday computing, light video, multiple displays. Not sufficient for: gaming, video editing, 3D rendering. When discrete GPU is installed, iGPU typically disabled.

AI-generated content raises unresolved IP questions. Current U.S. copyright law does not protect content generated entirely by AI without sufficient human authorship. Who owns AI output — the user? The AI company? The creators of training data? Still evolving legally. Practical guidance: treat AI output as a starting point, add human authorship and judgment before publishing or relying on it.

Connection drops and recovers periodically. Causes: flapping cable/connector (wiggle test — does connectivity drop when cable moved? = physical cable/connector issue), wireless interference or signal strength (weak/fluctuating signal), duplex mismatch (one side auto-negotiates to half-duplex = collisions), DHCP lease expiry issues, switch port flapping.
Change default credentials (first step). Disable unnecessary services. Segment on dedicated VLAN isolated from workstations. Keep firmware updated.

Displays IP configuration for all adapters. Key output: IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, DNS server. ipconfig /all: adds MAC address, DHCP server, DNS servers, DHCP enabled/disabled, lease obtained/expires. ipconfig /release: releases DHCP lease. ipconfig /renew: requests new DHCP lease. ipconfig /flushdns: clears local DNS resolver cache (fixes stale DNS entries).

32-bit address written as four octets in dotted decimal notation (e.g., 192.168.1.100). Each octet = 8 bits (0–255). IP address has two parts: network portion (determined by subnet mask) and host portion. Same network = same network portion.
Class A: 10.0.0.0/8. Class B: 172.16.0.0/12. Class C: 192.168.0.0/16. These are non-routable on the public internet (RFC 1918).

128-bit address. Written as 8 groups of 4 hex digits separated by colons: 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334. Compression rules: leading zeros in a group can be omitted (0db8 → db8), consecutive all-zero groups replaced with :: (once per address). Types: Global unicast (2000::/3) — routable internet. Link-local (fe80::/10) — auto-configured, non-routable, like APIPA but always present. Loopback: ::1. Multicast: FF00::/8.

SLAAC (Stateless Address Autoconfiguration): router sends RA (Router Advertisement) with network prefix; device generates host portion from MAC via EUI-64 (inserts ff:fe into the middle of MAC address, flips 7th bit). DHCPv6 (stateful): like DHCPv4, central server assigns addresses.

Debian-based distribution specifically designed for penetration testing and security research. Comes pre-loaded with hundreds of security tools (Wireshark, Metasploit, Nmap, etc.). Used by security professionals.

Ticket-based authentication. Default for Windows AD domains. KDC issues TGT at login → TGT used to request service tickets. Requires synchronized clocks — >5 minute drift causes auth failure. Port 88 TCP/UDP.

/etc/passwd: user account info (username, UID, GID, home dir, shell). "x" in password field points to /etc/shadow. /etc/shadow: encrypted password storage — readable only by root. /etc/hosts: static hostname-to-IP mappings, checked before DNS. /etc/fstab: filesystems to auto-mount at boot — errors prevent boot. /etc/resolv.conf: DNS server configuration (nameserver IP).
$USER — current username. $HOME — current user's home directory (/home/username). $PATH — directories searched for executables. $SHELL — current shell (/bin/bash). $PWD — current working directory.

%USERNAME% — logged-in username. %USERPROFILE% — path to current user's home directory (C:\Users\username). %APPDATA% — path to AppData\Roaming. %TEMP% / %TMP% — temp directory path. %PATH% — directories searched for executables. %COMPUTERNAME% — machine hostname. %SYSTEMROOT% — Windows directory (C:\Windows). %PROGRAMFILES% — Program Files (64-bit). %PROGRAMFILES(X86)% — Program Files (x86).

Laptop keyboards typically secured by small screws under the device or clips under the top bezel. Connects via flat ribbon cable to ZIF connector on motherboard. Replacement: release ZIF, remove keyboard, reverse process with new keyboard. Some ultrabooks have keyboards bonded to top case — replacement requires replacing the entire top assembly.

Membrane: dome-switch beneath each key, rubber membrane, quiet, inexpensive, mushy feel. Most office/OEM keyboards. Mechanical: individual switch per key (Cherry MX, Gateron, etc.). Tactile bump (Brown), Clicky (Blue), Linear (Red). Preferred for typing accuracy and longevity. Chiclet / scissors-switch: flat laptop-style keys, thin travel, used in ultrabooks and Apple keyboards. PS/2 connector (legacy, round DIN): keyboard-specific on older systems. USB: universal modern connection. Wireless: 2.4 GHz RF dongle or Bluetooth.
Built-in password/certificate manager. Stores passwords, certificates, private keys. Syncs across Apple devices via iCloud Keychain. Equivalent to Windows Credential Manager.
Records every keystroke. Captures passwords, card numbers, messages. Software or physical hardware form (inserted between keyboard and PC).

Repository of articles documenting known issues and their solutions. Articles created from resolved tickets (especially recurring issues). Format: problem description + root cause + resolution steps. Reduces repeat ticket escalation — front-line staff search KB before escalating. Self-service portal allows users to search KB before submitting ticket.

Keyboard-Video-Mouse switch. One set of keyboard, monitor, and mouse shared across 2+ computers. User switches between computers via hotkey or button. Available as hardware (HDMI/DP + USB) or software (network-based KVM). Common in server rooms for managing multiple servers from one console. IP KVM: network-connected, managed remotely.

Laptops vary significantly by manufacturer — always consult the service manual. General rules: remove battery first (or disconnect battery header on modern ultra-slim laptops). Use plastic pry tools to avoid scratching. Track screw sizes and locations (photo or label). Ribbon cables use ZIF (Zero Insertion Force) connectors — lift the locking tab before pulling, never yank.

Vertical lines or streaks on every page: dirty drum (streak at same location every ~94mm = drum circumference), scratched drum, or toner low. Clean drum or replace toner/drum unit. Ghost image (faint duplicate image offset from main print): fuser failing (not fully cleaning drum), worn drum unit. Replace fuser or drum. Toner not fused (smears when rubbed, especially when warm): fuser assembly failure — replace fuser. Speckled or smeared background (toner scattered on page): damaged photosensitive drum. Blank pages: toner empty, drum sealing tape not removed from new cartridge (new install issue), transfer roller failure.

Toner cartridge: contains toner powder (dry plastic + pigment) and often the drum in one replaceable unit. Drum/imaging unit: photosensitive cylinder — separate in some printers. Fuser assembly: heat + pressure roller that bonds toner to paper. Transfer roller/belt: transfers toner from drum to paper. Primary charge roller (PCR): replaces corona wire in modern laser printers — applies uniform charge to drum. Pick rollers/feed rollers: pull paper from tray. Separation pad: prevents multiple sheets feeding simultaneously.

1. Charging: primary corona wire or charge roller applies uniform negative charge to the photosensitive drum. 2. Exposing: laser beam neutralizes (exposes) charge on drum in image areas — where laser hits, charge drops (exposed areas become positively charged relative to background). 3. Developing: negatively charged toner particles are attracted to the relatively positive (exposed) areas of the drum. 4. Transferring: positively charged transfer roller or transfer belt attracts toner from drum onto negatively charged paper passing through. 5. Fusing: heated fuser roller and pressure roller melt toner into paper fibers permanently. 6. Cleaning: cleaning blade scrapes residual toner off drum, corona wire resets charge for next page.

LEGACY — Windows 7 feature. Loads the last successful registry hive (SYSTEM hive saved at last successful logon). Not applicable to Windows 10/11 in the same way — replaced by other recovery options. May still appear on exam in context of older OS troubleshooting.

Perimeter: bollards, fences, lighting. Access control: vestibule, badge readers, guards. Surveillance: CCTV, motion sensors, alarms. Equipment: cable locks, rack locks, cipher locks. Defense in depth — multiple layers means failure of one does not compromise everything.

TN (Twisted Nematic): fastest response time (1ms), lowest cost, poor viewing angles (colors shift at angles), poor color accuracy. Best for: budget laptops, gaming (if color accuracy not priority). IPS (In-Plane Switching): wide viewing angles (178°), accurate color reproduction, slightly slower response. Best for: professional use, color-critical work, general use. VA (Vertical Alignment): highest contrast ratio, wide viewing angles, slower response than TN. Rarely used in laptops.

Credentials from a breached app/service used against other services (users reuse passwords). Mobile apps with weak security may expose credentials via unencrypted local storage or insecure API. Mitigation: use unique passwords per service, enable MFA.
Standard users for daily work. Admin accounts only for administrative tasks. Limits blast radius of any compromise.
Grace period ~30 days: reduced functionality, data retained. After grace period: data may be deleted per platform retention policy. Renew before expiration to prevent disruption.

Running software without a valid license is copyright infringement. Consequences: legal liability (DMCA, civil suits), vendor audits (Microsoft BSA audits are common), fines. Software Asset Management (SAM) tracks licenses to ensure compliance.

Proper lifting prevents back injury: stand close to the load, bend at the knees (not waist), keep back straight, lift with leg muscles, keep load close to body, do not twist while carrying (turn feet, not torso), get help for heavy items (server racks, UPS units), use a dolly or lift for server equipment.

Exterior lighting improves surveillance camera effectiveness and deters opportunistic intruders. Security guards provide human judgment — verify identity visually, challenge unusual behavior, respond to incidents.

Apple proprietary connector (2012–2023). 8-pin reversible. Used on: older iPhones, iPads, AirPods, accessories. Replaced by USB-C in iPhone 15+, iPad Pro, and modern MacBooks. Exam context: recognize as Apple proprietary, not a standard.

IP assigned but internet not reachable. Check default gateway IP in ipconfig — must match router interface IP. Ping the gateway: no response = can't reach router (local network issue). Gateway responds but no internet: ISP-side issue or incorrect routing.
BIOS/UEFI → Bootloader (GRUB2) → Linux Kernel → systemd (init system, PID 1) → all other services and processes. systemd manages service startup, dependencies, and system state.

/ (root): top of the entire directory tree. /home: user home directories (/home/username). /etc: system configuration files (passwd, hosts, fstab, resolv.conf). /var: variable data — logs (/var/log), mail, print spools, databases. /usr: user programs and utilities (/usr/bin, /usr/lib). /bin and /sbin: essential system binaries (ls, cp, init). /tmp: temporary files — cleared on reboot. /dev: device files (disk = /dev/sda, terminal = /dev/tty). /proc: virtual filesystem for process and kernel information. /boot: kernel files and bootloader. /opt: optional/third-party software. /mnt and /media: mount points for external drives and removable media.
Open-source OS with hundreds of distributions. Linux kernel is the core; distros add package managers, desktop environments, and tools on top. ~80% of servers globally run Linux.

All-In-One (AIO) liquid cooler. Components: cold plate (contacts CPU), pump, tubing, radiator, fans. Pump circulates coolant from cold plate to radiator. Fans dissipate heat from radiator. Radiator sizes: 120mm (1 fan), 240mm (2 fans), 360mm (3 fans) — larger = more cooling capacity. Better than most air coolers for high-TDP CPUs. Factory sealed — not field-serviceable.

Type of generative AI trained on massive text corpora. Predict the next token in a sequence based on context. Capable of: answering questions, summarizing documents, writing and explaining code, drafting communications, troubleshooting assistance. Examples: GPT series, Claude, Gemini. Not databases — they generate probabilistic responses, not factual lookups.

Distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers. Algorithms: round-robin, least connections, IP hash, weighted. Provides: high availability (server failure = traffic redistributed), scalability (add servers to increase capacity), session persistence (sticky sessions — same client to same server). Hardware or software (HAProxy, Nginx, F5).

Manages local user accounts and group memberships. NOT available on Windows Home edition — Pro and higher only. Built-in groups: Administrators (full control), Users (standard), Guests (minimal), Power Users (legacy). Group membership determines access privileges. Create, modify, delete accounts; set passwords; configure account expiration.
Find My (iOS/macOS), Find My Device (Android). Must be ENABLED BEFORE loss — cannot activate retroactively. Functions: locate, sound alarm, lock, display message, remote wipe.
Dormant code triggered by a condition (date, event, user action). Often planted by insiders.

IPv4: 127.0.0.1 (entire 127.0.0.0/8 block is loopback). IPv6: ::1. Always refers to the local machine. Never crosses the network — used to test the TCP/IP stack is functioning. ping 127.0.0.1 = TCP/IP stack test (no network hardware involved).

Tests NIC or switch port by redirecting transmitted signal back to the receiver. Ethernet loopback: pins 1-3 and 2-6 crossed. If port tests OK with loopback but fails in actual use: suspect cable or far-end device.

Batch FOR loop: FOR %i IN (.txt) DO echo %i (iterates files). PowerShell ForEach-Object: Get-ChildItem | ForEach-Object { $_.Name }. Python for loop: for item in list:. Bash for loop: for file in .txt; do echo $file; done. Used for: processing files in bulk, creating multiple user accounts, automated repetitive tasks.
Writes zeros to every sector — overwrites data areas. Harder to recover but not impossible with forensic tools. Below secure wipe assurance level.

Small PCB slot directly on motherboard. Size designation: first two digits = width (mm), last two = length (mm). Most common: 2280 (22mm × 80mm). Also: 2242, 2260. Key types: M key (PCIe NVMe slot — most common), B key (SATA and some NVMe), B+M key (supports both SATA and NVMe). Must match motherboard slot keying. Check motherboard spec for supported protocols (SATA vs NVMe) before purchasing.
Whitelist/blacklist by MAC address. MAC addresses are SPOOFABLE — attacker sniffs authorized MACs and spoofs one. Adds friction but is not a strong control.

AI subset where systems learn patterns from large datasets without being explicitly programmed for each specific task. The model improves its performance through training on data. Types: supervised learning (labeled training data), unsupervised learning (finds patterns in unlabeled data), reinforcement learning (learns through reward/penalty feedback). Used in: spam filters, fraud detection, recommendation systems, image recognition.

.dmg (Disk Image): most common distribution. Opens as a virtual drive. Contains the .app bundle + Applications folder shortcut. User drags .app to /Applications — THAT is the install. The .dmg is a container, not the installer itself. Eject .dmg after install. .pkg (Package): complex installer like Windows .msi. Runs wizard, can install to multiple system locations, runs pre/post-install scripts, requires admin. .app (Application Bundle): self-contained directory that looks like one file. Contains binary, resources, metadata. Can run from any location but /Applications is standard.

/Applications: all installed apps, shared by all users. /Users: home directories for all user accounts (each has Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Music). /Library: system-wide support files, fonts, frameworks — requires admin to modify. /System: core OS files, kernel, drivers — protected by SIP (System Integrity Protection), cannot be modified even by admin/root. ~/Library (tilde = current user's home): per-user preferences, caches, app support data — hidden by default. Access: Option+click Go menu, or Cmd+Shift+G then type ~/Library.

Apple's proprietary desktop OS. Runs exclusively on Apple hardware (iMacs, Mac Mini, Mac Studio, Mac Pro, MacBooks) — enforced by EULA. Built on Unix-based Darwin kernel (similar behavior to Linux). Updates are free for supported hardware. Apple supports hardware for 6+ years. Default filesystem: APFS (optimized for SSDs, encryption, snapshots, shared storage pools).

App Store apps: long-press in Launchpad → click X. Other apps: drag .app from /Applications to Trash. NOTE: this does NOT remove associated files in ~/Library/Application Support and ~/Library/Preferences — need third-party uninstaller for complete removal.

Handles email transmission and storage. MTA (Mail Transfer Agent): SMTP — sends/relays email between servers (port 25). MDA (Mail Delivery Agent): delivers to user mailboxes. MUA (Mail User Agent): email client — retrieves via IMAP (143) or POP3 (110). SPF, DKIM, DMARC: email authentication records in DNS that reduce spoofing.

Scheduled time period (typically nights/weekends) when changes are made to minimize business impact. Agreed upon with business stakeholders. Change must complete (including rollback if needed) within the maintenance window.

Unexpected data usage (background exfiltration). Battery drain beyond normal use. Device running hot when idle. Unauthorized account access or charges. Pop-ups and ads appearing in system UI (outside app). Contacts, call logs, or photos accessed without permission. New apps appearing without user installation.

MDM profiles on iOS can configure VPN, Wi-Fi, email, and install root CA certificates. Attacker-installed malicious profiles can: route all traffic through attacker VPN, install rogue root CA enabling HTTPS interception, push malicious app configurations. Installed via social engineering or malicious website. Check: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management — remove any unrecognized profiles.

INVESTIGATE AND VERIFY. Confirm infection: slow performance, pop-ups, redirects, crashed programs, unusual network activity, missing/modified files, disabled AV. Document everything. Rule out hardware/software issues.
EDUCATE THE END USER. Explain how infection occurred. Teach safe browsing. Reinforce phishing and social engineering awareness. Users are the first line of defense and most common failure point.

QUARANTINE. DISCONNECT FROM NETWORK. Remove Ethernet cable, disable WiFi, disable Bluetooth. Prevents spread, C2 communication, payload download, data exfiltration. DO NOT POWER OFF — RAM evidence lost; some malware triggers destructive shutdown actions.
DISABLE SYSTEM RESTORE. Deletes all existing restore points (which may contain malware). Must happen BEFORE scanning. System Restore re-enabled in Step 9.
REMEDIATE. Begin active removal. Transfer updated definitions from clean machine via USB if internet unavailable.
UPDATE ANTI-MALWARE. Ensure scanner has most current definitions before full scan. New malware appears daily.

SCAN AND REMOVE. Run thorough scan in SAFE MODE (prevents malware loading during scan). F4 = minimal Safe Mode. F5 = Safe Mode with Networking. F6 = Safe Mode with Command Prompt. Rootkits: boot from external WinPE media to scan outside compromised OS.
REIMAGE IF NECESSARY. If malware cannot be fully removed, if system files too corrupted, or rootkit too embedded — clean OS reinstall. Back up user data first, scan before restoring.
SCHEDULE SCANS AND RUN UPDATES. Apply all Windows updates and patches. Enable automatic definition updates. Configure scheduled scans. Patch the vulnerability that allowed initial infection.
ENABLE SYSTEM RESTORE AND CREATE RESTORE POINT. Re-enable System Restore. Immediately create a new clean restore point as known-good baseline.
Mobile Application Management. Manages APPS only (not whole device). BYOD use case — containerizes corporate apps, leaves personal apps untouched.

Provide realistic timelines. Do not overpromise. If you do not know the answer, say so and commit to finding out — then follow through. Update the customer proactively if timelines change. Uncertainty communicated honestly builds more trust than false promises.

Assign a network share to a drive letter so it appears as a local drive. Method 1: File Explorer > This PC > Map Network Drive. Method 2: net use Z: \\server\share. Add /persistent:yes to reconnect at logon. Disconnect: net use Z: /delete.

Up to 4 primary partitions on MBR disk. Or 3 primary + 1 extended (which contains unlimited logical partitions). Extended partition is a container — it cannot store data directly. System partition (contains boot files) must be active and primary.

Mobile Device Management. Centrally manages mobile fleet. Capabilities: push config profiles, enforce security policies, install/remove apps, track inventory, monitor compliance, execute remote wipe. Examples: Microsoft Intune, VMware Workspace ONE, Jamf Pro.

MDM (Mobile Device Management): centralized platform to manage mobile devices at enterprise scale. Capabilities: enforce PIN/password policy, require encryption, remote wipe/lock, app deployment, VPN profile push, certificate distribution, BYOD containerization (separate work and personal profiles). BYOD: personal device used for work — MDM may manage a container rather than the entire device. Corporate-owned devices: full device management.
Managed Detection and Response. Third-party SOC monitors EDR telemetry 24/7. For organizations without internal security staff.

Something you KNOW: password, PIN, security question. Something you HAVE: TOTP token, authenticator app, SMS code, smart card. Something you ARE: fingerprint, facial recognition, retina, voice. TRUE MFA = factors from TWO OR MORE DIFFERENT CATEGORIES. Two passwords = NOT MFA.

Cloud-hosted email and productivity suite. Email via Exchange Online. Desktop client Outlook uses MAPI over HTTPS. IMAP/SMTP supported for third-party clients. Mailbox: 50-100 GB depending on license. Microsoft 365 apps: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint.
Business Basic: web/mobile apps only (no desktop Office), email, OneDrive, Teams. Business Standard: adds desktop Office apps. Business Premium: adds advanced security and device management.

MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output): uses multiple antennas to send/receive multiple data streams simultaneously on the same frequency — increases throughput to single device. Introduced in 802.11n. MU-MIMO (Multi-User MIMO): serves multiple devices simultaneously (not just one at a time). 802.11ac: DL MU-MIMO (4 streams down). 802.11ax: UL and DL MU-MIMO (8 streams).

Created automatically after BSOD. Located at C:\Windows\Minidump\. Contain stop code, loaded drivers, and call stack at time of crash. Analyzed with WinDbg or uploaded to third-party tools. Event Viewer > System log also records stop error event.
Malware may delete or rename system files to cause instability or prevent security tools from running. SFC /scannow repairs corrupted/missing system files.
Shows all open windows and virtual desktops (Spaces). Manage multiple desktops for workspace organization.

Microsoft Management Console — framework hosting administrative snap-ins. Launch blank MMC with mmc.exe, then add snap-ins. Most tools have pre-built .msc shortcuts: devmgmt.msc, diskmgmt.msc, eventvwr.msc, taskschd.msc, lusrmgr.msc, gpedit.msc, perfmon.msc, services.msc, compmgmt.msc.

Smartphone: primary personal computing device, cellular + Wi-Fi + Bluetooth, voice/data/apps. Tablet: larger touchscreen, Wi-Fi (and optional LTE), productivity and media. E-reader (Kindle, Kobo): E-ink display — reflective, not emissive, easier on eyes for reading, low power (weeks per charge), poor in dark without frontlight. Smartwatch: wearable, pairs to smartphone via Bluetooth, health sensors (HR, SpO2, ECG), limited standalone apps. GPS device: dedicated navigation, receives GNSS signals (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo), preloaded maps. Fitness tracker: step counting, sleep tracking, HR monitoring, usually simpler than smartwatch.

iOS (Apple): closed ecosystem, apps from App Store only (no sideloading without developer/enterprise enrollment or jailbreak), annual major updates, 6+ years of support, tightly integrated hardware/software. Android (Google): open-source Linux base, Google Play Store primary + sideloading possible (Unknown Sources/Allow from this source), fragmented update support (depends on manufacturer and carrier).

NFC-based: Apple Pay (iOS), Google Pay/Wallet (Android), Samsung Pay. Device stores encrypted token (not actual card number). Requires: NFC-enabled device, NFC-capable payment terminal (contactless symbol). Authentication: biometric (fingerprint/Face ID) or PIN before payment. Secure Element: dedicated hardware chip stores payment credentials, isolated from main OS.

Fake security warnings on mobile claiming device is infected, demanding payment or app download to "clean" it. Often delivered via malicious website pop-up or ad. Does NOT indicate actual infection — it is social engineering. Never call the provided number or download the suggested app. Close the browser tab.

Non-modular: all cables permanently attached — unused cables bundle inside case (clutters airflow). Semi-modular: main cables permanent, extras detachable. Fully modular: all cables detachable — only connect what's needed. Cleaner builds, better airflow. Slightly higher cost. Modular cables from different PSU brands are usually NOT interchangeable — using wrong cables can damage equipment.

4-pin PSU connector — large plastic plug with 2 yellow (+12V), 1 red (+5V), 1 black (ground). Powers older IDE drives, fans, optical drives, accessories. Being replaced by SATA power in modern systems. Adapters convert Molex to SATA power.

ATX: 305×244mm. Standard for desktop PCs. 4+ PCIe slots, multiple RAM slots, full I/O. Most common. Micro-ATX (mATX): 244×244mm. Fewer PCIe slots (typically 2–3). Fits ATX and mATX cases. Good balance of size and expansion. Mini-ITX: 170×170mm. 1 PCIe x16 slot, 2 RAM slots. Very compact — for small form factor (SFF) builds. E-ATX: larger than ATX — high-end desktop (HEDT), server, workstation.

Motion sensors detect movement in restricted zones and trigger alerts or alarms. Alarm systems notify security personnel of unauthorized access events. Used in server rooms, data centers, and secure storage areas.

Optical mouse: uses LED + CMOS sensor to detect surface movement. Laser mouse: uses laser — works on more surfaces including glass. DPI (dots per inch): sensitivity setting. Higher DPI = cursor moves more with less physical movement. Gaming mice: adjustable DPI, extra buttons, polling rate. Trackball: stationary body, ball rotates — alternative for limited desk space or accessibility. Touchpad: capacitive surface on laptops.

Older Windows built-in remote assistance tool. User creates an invitation file (.msrcincident) and sends to support technician. Technician opens the file to connect. Requires firewall rule (port 135 + dynamic ports). More complex than Quick Assist — largely superseded by Quick Assist in modern environments.

Created for EU antitrust compliance — Microsoft required to offer versions without bundled media software. "N" = Not with Media Player. Excludes: Windows Media Player, Music, Video, Voice Recorder, Skype. All other features intact. Microsoft offers downloadable Media Feature Pack to restore missing components. N editions exist for Home, Pro, Enterprise, and Education.

Maps private IP addresses to public IP for internet communication. PAT (Port Address Translation / NAT Overload): maps many private IPs to one public IP using unique port numbers per session — most common home/SMB implementation. NAT table tracks active sessions for return traffic. Limitation: breaks some protocols that embed IP addresses in payload (IPsec, SIP).

Displays active network connections and listening ports. Key flags: -a (all connections + listening ports), -n (show numeric IPs instead of resolving names — faster), -o (show PID for each connection — cross-reference with Task Manager), -b (show executable for each connection). Use to detect unauthorized connections, identify which process is using a port, verify services are listening.

Physical diagram: shows actual physical connections — cables, ports, patch panels, rack layouts, physical device locations. Logical diagram: shows IP addressing, VLANs, routing paths, security zones — how data flows. Both are critical documentation. Should be kept current — outdated diagrams are worse than none (false confidence).

Control Panel > Network and Sharing Center > Advanced sharing settings. Turn on/off network discovery, file/printer sharing per network profile. Windows Firewall must allow "File and Printer Sharing" exception for sharing to work.

Windows classifies each network as Domain, Private, or Public. Domain: auto-detected when joined to AD domain, least restrictive firewall profile, management tools have access. Private: user-designated home/trusted network, enables network discovery and file sharing, moderate firewall rules. Public: new/unknown networks (coffee shop, hotel), MOST restrictive, disables discovery and sharing, most common default for new connections. Profile determines Windows Firewall rule behavior.
VLANs separate IoT, guest, and workstation traffic. Limits lateral movement after compromise.

Virtual switch (vSwitch): connects VMs to each other and to physical network. Network modes: NAT (VM gets private IP, shares host IP for internet — most common for Type 2), Bridged (VM gets its own IP on physical network — appears as real machine on LAN), Host-only (VM can only communicate with host, isolated from external network).

Maximum range: 4 cm (approximately). Frequency: 13.56 MHz. Uses: contactless payment (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay), tap-to-pair (speaker, headphones), transit cards, access badges, small data transfers. Passive NFC tags: no battery, powered by reader's field. Active NFC: both devices have NFC radios. Security: short range provides inherent physical security.

RDP security feature requiring the user to authenticate BEFORE the full remote desktop session is established. Authentication challenge happens at OS level, not within the remote session. Benefit: reduces attack surface — unauthenticated users cannot reach the Windows login screen (which could be attacked). Reduces BlueKeep-type vulnerabilities. Enable in System Properties > Remote > "Allow connections only from computers running Remote Desktop with NLA."

Network scanner — discovers live hosts and open ports. Syntax: nmap [target IP or range]. -sn: ping scan (host discovery only). -p [ports]: specific port scan. -sV: service version detection. -O: OS detection. Used for: network inventory, security auditing, verifying firewall rules. Use only on networks you are authorized to scan.

Check: airplane mode off, SIM card seated properly (remove/reinsert), correct APN settings for carrier, carrier coverage in area. Reset network settings (erases Wi-Fi passwords, Bluetooth pairings, VPN settings — prompts re-entry). Contact carrier for SIM replacement if SIM hardware issue.

Check: monitor power on, video cable firmly connected at both ends, correct input selected on monitor (HDMI 1, DP 1, etc.), try different cable, try different port on GPU, test with known-good monitor. On laptop: check Fn key display toggle (Fn+F4 or similar — switches between internal, external, or both). If discrete GPU suspected: try integrated graphics output (requires removing discrete GPU).

term: No internet access but LAN works
definition: Can ping gateway and local devices, cannot reach internet. Causes: default gateway pointing to wrong IP, ISP outage, router WAN connection failure (check router admin page), DNS failure (can ping 8.8.8.8 but not google.com), firewall blocking outbound traffic. Test: ping 8.8.8.8 — if succeeds, DNS is the issue. If fails, routing/ISP issue.

Step 1: Check physical — Ethernet cable plugged in, switch port link light green. Step 2: ipconfig — check IP address. 169.254.x.x = APIPA = DHCP failure. Valid IP = DHCP working. Step 3: ping 127.0.0.1 — TCP/IP stack functional. Step 4: ping default gateway — local network connectivity. Step 5: ping external IP (8.8.8.8) — internet routing. Step 6: ping hostname (google.com) — DNS resolution. Each failed step localizes the problem.

System powers on (fans spin, lights on) but no display and no beep: check display cable and monitor first (test known-good monitor). Reseat RAM — most common cause of no POST. Reseat GPU. Check 24-pin ATX and 8-pin CPU power connectors seated fully. Clear CMOS (jumper on motherboard or remove CMOS battery 30 seconds). Try single RAM stick in slot A1/DIMM1. If still no POST → likely CPU or motherboard failure.

DNS query tool. Default: queries configured DNS server. Syntax: nslookup hostname. Change DNS server: nslookup hostname [dns-server-ip]. Reverse lookup: nslookup [IP address]. Set type: set type=MX for mail records, set type=AAAA for IPv6. Tests DNS resolution without system cache influence when using specific server.

New Technology File System — Windows default for internal drives. Features: journaling (logs changes before writing = crash recovery), file-level permissions (ACLs), EFS encryption support, audit trails, disk quotas, hard links, symbolic links, compression. Max file size: 16 TB. Max volume: up to 256 TB practical. Required for BitLocker and EFS.
Full Control, Modify, Read & Execute, List Folder Contents, Read, Write. Apply for local AND network access. Security tab in Properties.

Synchronizes clocks across network devices. Port 123 UDP. Stratum hierarchy: Stratum 0 (atomic clock/GPS reference), Stratum 1 (directly connected to Stratum 0), Stratum 2 (syncs from Stratum 1). Client syncs from Stratum 1 or 2 NTP servers. Critical for: Kerberos authentication (tickets invalid if time skew >5 minutes), log correlation, certificate validity, scheduled tasks. Windows uses W32TM service.

PCIe-based storage protocol designed specifically for SSDs. Replaces AHCI (designed for spinning disks). Dramatically faster than SATA: PCIe 3.0 x4 NVMe: ~3,500 MB/s sequential read. PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe: ~7,000 MB/s. SATA SSD: ~550 MB/s max. Uses M.2 M-key slot or PCIe AIC. Identified in BIOS as NVMe device (not SATA).

Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access. Divides a single channel into smaller sub-channels (Resource Units — RUs) serving multiple clients simultaneously on the same channel. Dramatically improves efficiency in high-density environments. More efficient than OFDM (which serves one device per channel at a time).
When an account is disabled/deleted on-premises AD, Azure AD Connect automatically disables/deletes the corresponding cloud account on next sync — critical for access revocation during offboarding.

Self-emissive — each pixel produces its own light. No backlight required. Advantages: true blacks (pixel turns completely off), infinite contrast ratio, wide color gamut, thinner panel. Disadvantages: burn-in risk (static elements like taskbars can permanently ghost), more expensive, potential brightness limitations. AMOLED = Active Matrix OLED (used in mobile devices).
Attacker between client and server. Intercepts, reads, and may modify traffic both directions. Via: ARP poisoning, DNS spoofing, rogue AP.

Creates local OneDrive folder (default: C:\Users\username\OneDrive). Syncs to cloud. Selective sync: choose which folders mirror locally. Files On-Demand: files appear in Explorer with cloud icon but no local storage until opened — reduces local disk use. Bandwidth throttling available to limit sync client network consumption. Troubleshooting sync: check internet connectivity, verify account credentials, check storage quota (full quota stops sync), look for unsupported characters in filenames, pause/resume sync client.

Disc not recognized: dirty/scratched disc (clean with lint-free cloth outward from center). Drive tray ejects then retracts: disc format not supported or disc damage. Drive not detected: check SATA/USB connection, try different disc type.

CD-ROM: 700 MB capacity. DVD: 4.7 GB (single-layer), 8.5 GB (dual-layer). Blu-ray: 25 GB (single-layer), 50 GB (dual-layer). BD-R (write once), BD-RE (rewritable). Modern PCs often omit optical drive — available as external USB. CD speeds: 1x = 150 KB/s; DVD 1x = 1,385 KB/s; Blu-ray 1x = 4.5 MB/s.

Windows (~75% desktop market share, proprietary). Linux (open-source, ~80% of servers, hundreds of distros). macOS (Apple hardware only, Unix-based Darwin kernel, free updates, 6+ year hardware support). Chrome OS (Google, Linux-derived, web-centered, Chromebooks, runs Android APKs, sub-5-second boot). Mobile: iOS (iPhones), iPadOS (adds multitasking vs iOS), Android (open-source, Linux-based, ~72% global mobile market share).

Common causes of failed OS updates: (1) Insufficient storage — OS update requires free space (often 2–4 GB). (2) Battery below threshold — most mobile OS updates require 50% battery minimum; plug in before updating. (3) Connectivity — requires stable Wi-Fi (updates too large for cellular on most devices). (4) Device compatibility — some OS versions require minimum hardware specs; old devices may not receive updates.

EOL applications receive no security patches — any vulnerability found after EOL is permanently exploitable. Running EOL software = same risk as running EOL OS. Isolate, plan replacement, prioritize upgrade.

Phone becomes uncomfortably hot during charging, gaming, or extended use. Causes: ambient heat, direct sunlight, intensive apps (gaming, video encoding), background processes, charging while under load. Device may trigger thermal throttling (slows down) or emergency shutdown. Remediation: remove from sunlight, close apps, stop charging temporarily, remove case, let cool.

CPU thermal throttling: system slows dramatically under load. Unexpected shutdown at high load. Fan runs at maximum speed. Temperatures verified via HWInfo64 or BIOS. Common causes: dried thermal paste, clogged heat sink with dust, fan failure, inadequate case airflow. Fix: clean dust, replace thermal paste, verify all fans operational.

Image appears larger than screen (edges cut off) = overscan. Common when connecting PC to HDTV via HDMI. Fix: disable overscan in TV picture settings or GPU driver (AMD: HDMI Scaling, NVIDIA: Adjust Desktop Size and Position). Image smaller than screen with black border = underscan. Adjust scaling in GPU driver.

sudo apt update: refreshes package list. sudo apt upgrade: installs all available updates. sudo apt install package-name: installs a package. sudo apt remove package-name: removes a package. sudo apt autoremove: removes unused dependencies.
sudo dnf install package-name. sudo dnf update. sudo dnf remove package-name. yum is the older version; dnf is the modern replacement on Fedora/RHEL 8+.

TN (Twisted Nematic): fastest response time (1ms GTG), lowest cost, poor viewing angles (colors shift beyond ~45°), mediocre color reproduction. Preferred for: competitive gaming where speed > color. IPS (In-Plane Switching): wide viewing angles (178° horizontal and vertical), accurate color, slower response than TN (4–5ms, though fast IPS panels now approach 1ms). Best for: professional use, photo/video editing, general consumer use. VA (Vertical Alignment): highest static contrast ratio (3000:1+ vs IPS ~1000:1), wide viewing angles, slower response than TN/IPS — ghosting risk. Best for: mixed use, movies. OLED: self-emissive, instant response (0.1ms), true blacks, near-infinite contrast. Risk: burn-in from static elements.

Clear using printer's jam clearing procedure (never force paper — tears and leaves fragments). Check all areas: input tray, transport path, fuser area (careful — fuser is hot). Remove all paper fragments before resuming printing. Recurring jams: worn pick rollers (clean with IPA or replace), incorrect paper weight, damp/humid paper, overfilled tray. Multifeeding (multiple sheets at once): worn separation pad — clean or replace.

No fans — relies on heatsink surface area and natural convection. Used for: low-power CPUs (NAS, embedded systems), network equipment, some M.2 NVMe heatsinks. Silent operation. Requires adequate case ventilation.

Generate and store unique passwords per site. Built-in (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) or third-party (Bitwarden, 1Password, Dashlane). Eliminates credential reuse. Auto-fill won't work on fake lookalike domains — reduces phishing success.
Length (8+ minimum, 12+ recommended). Complexity (upper/lower/number/symbol). History (prevent reuse). Modern NIST: prioritize length and uniqueness over mandatory rotation.
One common password tried against many accounts, rotating through accounts to stay below lockout threshold. Mitigated by MFA and lockout monitoring.

Passive device in rack — organizes and labels cable runs from wall outlets/jacks to central rack location. Punchdown blocks on rear accept cable runs. Front: RJ-45 jacks connect to switch via short patch cables. Creates organized, labeled, manageable cable infrastructure. 1U = 24 ports standard.

Combines ping and tracert. First traces route (like tracert), then sends hundreds of pings to each hop over ~90 seconds. Reports per-hop packet loss percentage and RTT statistics. More informative than tracert for intermittent issues. Long runtime (~2 minutes).

term: PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard)
definition: Industry standard (not law) mandating security controls for any organization that processes, stores, or transmits credit/debit card data. Requirements: network segmentation, encryption of cardholder data, access control, audit logging, vulnerability management, regular security testing. Non-compliance can result in fines and loss of card processing privileges.

PCI Express. x16 slot: longest, used for GPU. x8 slot: intermediate. x4 slot: shorter. x1 slot: shortest, used for expansion cards (sound, NIC, RAID). Versions: PCIe 3.0 (1 GB/s per lane), 4.0 (2 GB/s per lane), 5.0 (4 GB/s per lane). Backward compatible — a PCIe 3.0 card in a PCIe 4.0 slot runs at PCIe 3.0 speed. Physical slot size vs electrical lanes can differ (x16 slot physically, x4 electrically = runs GPU at x4 bandwidth).

Hundreds of configurable performance counters. Data Collector Sets allow scheduled collection and report generation. Use for baseline performance metrics and long-term analysis — more powerful than Task Manager for capacity planning.

Task Manager tabs: Performance (CPU/RAM/Disk/Network graphs), Processes (all running processes with resource usage), Details (per-process PID, CPU %, memory, I/O — more granular than Processes tab), Startup (programs that launch at boot — previously in msconfig). High CPU/RAM/Disk = identify offending process in Processes tab, right-click > End Task or investigate the process.

Never argue with a customer. Never be judgmental about their technical knowledge. Never discuss a customer's personal issues with other technicians. Never exceed authorized scope (do not access systems beyond what you are authorized to).

Health information linked to an individual — any PII in a healthcare context (diagnoses, treatment records, prescriptions, insurance info, lab results). Protected under HIPAA in the United States. Applies to covered entities (healthcare providers, insurers, clearinghouses) and their business associates.
Email-based social engineering. Spoofed sender/domain, malicious link or attachment, credential harvesting on fake login page. Uses urgency and authority. Look-alike domains (micros0ft.com).

Webcam kill switch: physical slider or button disconnects webcam power — LED indicator shows status. Microphone kill switch: hardware disconnect for microphone array. Privacy screen: built-in or attachable polarizing filter — narrows viewing angle so only person directly in front can see content.
Lock router in room/closet. Reset button restores factory defaults — bypasses all security configuration.

Any data that can identify a specific individual: name, Social Security Number, date of birth, address, phone number, email address, biometric data, IP address (context-dependent), account numbers. Organizations have legal obligations to protect PII. Exposure triggers breach notification requirements. Technicians must handle PII with minimum necessary access.

Tests ICMP reachability between source and destination. Reports round-trip time (RTT) and packet loss. Divide-and-conquer troubleshooting sequence: (1) ping 127.0.0.1 = TCP/IP stack working. (2) ping [own IP] = NIC and local stack. (3) ping [gateway] = local network connectivity. (4) ping [external IP like 8.8.8.8] = internet routing. (5) ping [hostname] = DNS resolution. Firewall may block ICMP — no response ≠ always unreachable.

Plenum space: air-handling space (above ceiling tiles, below raised floors) used for HVAC airflow. Plenum-rated cable (CMP rating): low-smoke, fire-retardant jacket — required by fire code in plenum spaces. Burns slower and produces less toxic smoke than standard PVC jacket. Non-plenum (CMR — riser rated): standard for vertical runs between floors in conduit. More flexible and less expensive than plenum.

Delivers power and data over standard CAT5e/CAT6 cable. Powered Device (PD) receives power from Power Sourcing Equipment (PSE — PoE switch or injector). Standards: 802.3af (PoE): 15.4W per port — IP phones, basic cameras. 802.3at (PoE+): 30W — more capable cameras, APs. 802.3bt (PoE++): 60W/100W — high-power APs, PTZ cameras, thin clients. PoE injector: adds PoE to non-PoE switch for single device.
Enabled by default in modern browsers. Blocks malvertising pop-ups.
Popups or ads appearing when no browser is open = strong indicator of adware or malware. Legitimate software does not generate OS-level popups advertising products. Run full malware scan.

Post Office Protocol v3. Retrieves email from server to client. Downloads messages and typically deletes from server (configurable). Not synchronized — email exists on one device only after download. Legacy protocol largely replaced by IMAP for modern use. POP3S (encrypted) = port 995.

Internet Message Access Protocol. Email retrieval with server synchronization. Email stays on server — accessible from multiple devices in sync. Read/unread, folders synchronized. IMAPS (encrypted) = port 993. Preferred over POP3 for multi-device access.

Simple Network Management Protocol. Port 161: queries to devices (GET, SET requests). Port 162: traps from devices (unsolicited alerts to manager). Community strings = passwords (public/private in SNMPv1/v2). SNMPv3 adds encryption and strong authentication. Used for: network device monitoring, performance data collection, fault alerting.

File Transfer Protocol. Unencrypted. Port 21 = control channel (commands). Port 20 = data channel (active mode). SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) uses port 22 — encrypted, completely different protocol from FTP. FTPS (FTP Secure) = FTP + TLS. Use SFTP or FTPS instead of plain FTP for security.

Secure Shell. Encrypted remote CLI access. Replaces Telnet. Authentication: password or public key. Common clients: PuTTY (Windows), OpenSSH (all platforms). Also tunnels other protocols (VNC via SSH tunnel, X11 forwarding). Key-based auth: generate key pair, place public key on server, keep private key secure.

Unencrypted remote CLI. Transmits all data including credentials in plaintext — trivially intercepted. Legacy protocol — replaced by SSH. Only acceptable on isolated, trusted networks (e.g., console management network). Always the wrong answer on exam security questions.

Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. Sending email between mail servers (MTA to MTA). Also used by email clients to submit outgoing mail (ports 465/587 for SSL/TLS submission). SMTP does not retrieve email — only sends/relays.
Remote Desktop Protocol. Graphical Windows remote desktop. Encrypted. Covered in Core 2 4.9. Should NOT be exposed directly to internet — use VPN + RDP instead.

Lightweight Directory Access Protocol. Queries and modifies directory services (Active Directory). Port 389 = unencrypted. Port 636 = LDAPS (LDAP over TLS, encrypted). Applications authenticate to AD via LDAP queries.

HTTP over TLS. All traffic encrypted. Server presents TLS certificate (CA-signed). Client verifies certificate validity (not expired, CA trusted, hostname matches). Padlock icon in browser. Port 443 = always use for any web service transmitting sensitive data.

Server Message Block. Windows file and printer sharing. Used by: Windows file shares (\\server\share), Active Directory, print spooler. Target of infamous exploits (EternalBlue/WannaCry used SMB vulnerability). Should be blocked at network perimeter — not exposed to internet.

Domain Name System. Resolves hostnames to IP addresses. UDP for standard queries (fast, single packet). TCP for zone transfers (large data) and when response exceeds 512 bytes. Hierarchical: root → TLD → authoritative name server → local resolver cache. Record types: A (hostname → IPv4), AAAA (hostname → IPv6), MX (mail server), CNAME (alias), PTR (IP → hostname, reverse), NS (name server), TXT (verification, SPF, DKIM).

Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol. UDP. Server listens on 67, client sends from 68. DORA process: Discover (client broadcasts) → Offer (server proposes IP) → Request (client accepts) → Acknowledge (server confirms). Assigns: IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, DNS server, lease time. Scope: pool of available IPs. Exclusion: IPs within scope that are NOT assigned by DHCP (reserved for static devices). Reservation: specific IP always assigned to specific MAC address.
Hypertext Transfer Protocol. Unencrypted web traffic. Plaintext — all content including session cookies visible to network observers. Being replaced by HTTPS.

Switch port rapidly coming up and down — check event log for repeated link up/down events on same port. Causes: failing NIC, faulty cable, faulty SFP transceiver, duplex mismatch causing errors that trigger error-disable. Test with different cable and different port.
Restricts which MAC addresses can connect to a physical switch port. Dynamic (learn first MAC seen) or static (manually configured). Violation actions: restrict, shutdown, protect.

Email client submission (outgoing email from client to mail server). Port 465: SMTPS (implicit TLS — TLS from the start). Port 587: SMTP with STARTTLS (starts unencrypted, upgrades to TLS). Most modern email clients use port 587.

Firmware diagnostic run at startup to verify hardware. Tests: CPU, RAM, video, storage controllers, keyboard. Results: beep codes (vary by BIOS manufacturer — AMI, Award, Phoenix) or POST diagnostic codes on LCD on high-end boards. Common: 1 short beep = POST success (some BIOSes). Continuous/repeating beeps = RAM failure. Blank screen, no beep = GPU or power issue. No beep at all = no speaker connected or speaker failed.

Surge: brief overvoltage spike (lightning, switching loads). Sag/brownout: sustained undervoltage — can damage motors and power supplies. Blackout: complete power loss. Noise: electrical interference on power line. Clean power: stable voltage with no fluctuations. UPS handles all of these for protected equipment.

System won't turn on: check power cable, wall outlet, PSU switch on rear (if present). Test with known-good PSU. Paper clip test: short the 24-pin green wire (PS_ON) to black (ground) — if PSU fan spins, basic PSU function works (but doesn't test under load). Random shutdown or won't stay on: test PSU wattage adequacy, check 12V rail voltage with multimeter. Voltage readings outside ±5% of spec = failing PSU.

Three plans: Balanced (default — dynamic performance), Power Saver (reduced performance for battery), High Performance (max CPU speed, more power). Sleep: session in RAM, near-instant resume, volatile (power loss destroys session). Hibernate: RAM written to hiberfil.sys, powered off completely, slower resume (15-30s), survives power loss, requires disk space = installed RAM. Enable/disable: powercfg /hibernate on|off. Hybrid Sleep: combines both — writes RAM to disk but stays in Sleep for fast resume; recovers from disk if power fails. Fast Startup: saves kernel/driver state to hiberfil.sys on shutdown for faster next boot — disable when troubleshooting boot issues or with dual-boot.

Surge protector: MOV (Metal Oxide Varistor) absorbs brief overvoltage spikes. MOV degrades — surge protectors need periodic replacement. UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply): battery backup + surge protection. Protects against: power loss (provides time to save work and shut down), voltage sags, surges, line noise. Line-interactive UPS: handles voltage fluctuations without switching to battery. Online (double conversion) UPS: always runs through inverter — cleanest power, highest cost.

Controls which scripts are allowed to run. Default: Restricted — no PowerShell scripts can run. RemoteSigned: local scripts run freely; downloaded scripts require digital signature. Unrestricted: all scripts run (not recommended). Check policy: Get-ExecutionPolicy. Change: Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser. Policy set by GPO in enterprise environments.

Toner (laser printer powder) is a fine particulate — inhalation hazard. PPE: disposable gloves, safety glasses, N95 or P100 respirator mask. Cleaning: use a specialized antistatic toner vacuum (regular vacuums scatter toner into the air and can generate ignition sparks from static). Do not use compressed air (creates cloud of inhaled toner).
Fabricated scenario to manipulate target into action. The foundational technique underlying most social engineering.

Manages shared printers over the network. Windows Print and Document Services role. Clients connect to printer via UNC path (\\printserver\printername). Spooler service manages print queue. IPP (Internet Printing Protocol) port 631 — cross-platform printing.

Windows service (Print Spooler / spoolsv.exe) queues print jobs and manages communication with printer. Spool files stored in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS\. Spooler crash = no printing from any application. Fix: net stop spooler → delete contents of spool\PRINTERS → net start spooler.

Print spooler (spoolsv.exe) manages print queue. Crash symptoms: all print jobs stuck, no new jobs processed, printer offline in queue. Fix: (1) net stop spooler (2) delete all files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS\ (NOT the folder itself) (3) net start spooler. Or: Services.msc → Print Spooler → Restart. Print jobs stuck in queue: cancel all jobs, restart spooler, resubmit job.

USB: direct local connection to single computer. Ethernet (RJ-45): wired network connection — shared by all users on network. Wi-Fi: wireless network connection. Bluetooth: short-range, typically for mobile printing. NFC: tap to print (mobile). Cloud printing: Google Cloud Print (deprecated), Apple AirPrint, Mopria (Android) — print directly from mobile devices.

Software translating application print commands to printer-specific language. PCL (Printer Command Language): HP standard, widely compatible. PostScript (PS): Adobe, preferred for graphics/design (resolution-independent). Proprietary: manufacturer-specific drivers for full feature access. Driver must match OS and printer model exactly — wrong driver = no print or incorrect output.

Wrong driver = incorrect output, missing features, or no communication. Generic driver: Windows may install generic PCL driver — works for basic printing but loses printer-specific features. Fix: download correct model-specific driver from manufacturer website. After driver install: test print. If driver corrupt: uninstall driver, run manufacturer uninstaller, reinstall clean driver.

Windows shows printer as "Offline" even when physically connected and powered on. Check: printer not in sleep mode (wake it), USB/network cable connected, IP address changed (network printers — check printer IP vs Windows port config), correct printer driver. Fix: delete printer from Windows, re-add. Restart Print Spooler service. For network printer: ping printer IP to verify connectivity.

P1/Critical: complete business outage, major revenue impact, all hands — immediate response. P2/High: significant degradation affecting many users. P3/Medium: single user affected, workaround exists. P4/Low: cosmetic, informational, enhancement request. SLA defines response and resolution time targets per priority level.

Do not look at, read, or access data/files not directly relevant to the support issue. Minimize what you open on the user's screen. Do not shoulder-surf passwords. If you encounter sensitive personal information or confidential business data, treat it as unseen. Do not discuss what you observed with colleagues.

Polarizing screen overlay that narrows effective viewing angle to ~30° — only person directly in front sees image; people at an angle see dark/black screen. Clip-on or adhesive. Used in open offices, public spaces. Reduces screen brightness.

term: Privacy risks of public AI tools
definition: Public AI services (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Copilot, Gemini) may use input data for model training or retain it on vendor servers. Entering sensitive data creates privacy and security risks: employee PII, customer PHI, proprietary business processes, trade secrets, financial data, source code. Many organizations prohibit entering sensitive company data into public AI tools via AUP.

Chrome: Incognito. Edge: InPrivate. Firefox: Private Window. DOES: prevents local history/cookies/form data from saving after session. DOES NOT: anonymize, hide from ISP/employer/websites, prevent malware, hide from network monitoring. Only prevents LOCAL session data saving.

Mainstream support (~5 years): feature updates + bug fixes + security patches. Extended support (~3-5 years more): security patches only — no new features, no non-security bug fixes. End of Life (EOL): no patches of any kind. Known vulnerabilities permanently unpatched. Windows 10 Home/Pro reached EOL October 2025. Correct response to EOL system: isolate from internet, segment from sensitive network, prioritize replacement.

term: Professionalism in body language and appearance
definition: Punctual. Professional attire (organization-dependent). Knock before entering. Introduce yourself. Maintain appropriate eye contact. Do not use personal devices (phone) while working with a customer — signals disrespect and inattention.

DLP (Digital Light Processing): single or three DMD (Digital Micromirror Device) chips. Single-chip uses color wheel — may cause "rainbow effect" in some viewers. High contrast, compact. Good for: business presentations. LCD projector: three liquid crystal panels (one per color), bright, accurate color, no rainbow effect. Laser projector: laser light source instead of lamp. Long lifespan (20,000+ hours), instant on/off, no lamp replacement. Higher cost. Brightness measured in lumens (projectors) — higher lumen rating for brighter rooms.

No image: check cable, input source selected, lamp (if lamp-based — dim or no light = lamp needs replacement after ~2000–5000 hours). Color incorrect: color calibration or lamp degradation. Overheating: clean filter/vents. Blurry: focus adjustment, lens dirty.

Intermediary between clients and internet. Forward proxy: clients route traffic through proxy for caching (bandwidth saving), content filtering, logging, anonymization. Reverse proxy: sits in front of web servers — load balancing, SSL termination, caching, WAF functionality. Transparent proxy: intercepts traffic without client configuration.

Settings > Network and Internet > Proxy. Or browser-level proxy settings. Proxy server acts as intermediary between client and internet — used for content filtering, caching, monitoring in corporate environments. Configured with server address and port. Can be enforced via Group Policy.

24-pin ATX: main motherboard power connector. 4+4 pin (8-pin) EPS/CPU: CPU power connector — plugs into CPU power header. Critical — system will not boot without this. 6+2 pin PCIe: GPU power. High-end GPUs may require 2× 8-pin or 16-pin (12VHPWR for PCIe 5.0 cards). SATA power (15-pin, L-shaped): storage drives, optical drives. Molex 4-pin: fans, legacy devices, adapters.
ATX: standard for desktop cases. 150×86mm width. SFX/SFX-L: small form factor cases. TFX: thin/low-profile cases. Flex ATX: very small, used in 1U rackmount. Must match case specification.

Power Supply Unit converts AC mains power (120V/60Hz in North America, 230V/50Hz in Europe) to DC voltages used by computer components: +12V (CPU, GPU, motors), +5V (older components, USB power), +3.3V (modern components), -12V (legacy serial ports), +5VSB (standby — keeps USB power when PC off).

Formal process to evaluate, approve, schedule, and document changes to IT systems. Prevents unplanned outages, ensures rollback plans exist, maintains documentation, enables impact analysis before making changes. Governed by Change Advisory Board. All production changes go through this process.
Malicious URL hidden in QR code. Appears in emails, printed materials, or as sticker over legitimate QR code. URL invisible to humans without scanning device.

Built into Windows 10/11. Two roles: Presenter (user being helped — shares screen) and Helper (support technician — views/controls screen). Helper receives a 6-digit code from Microsoft cloud service. Presenter enters code to initiate session. Helper can view or take full control (requires presenter approval). No additional software needed. Requires Microsoft account for helper. Good for quick consumer-level support.

Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service. AAA protocol. UDP ports 1812 (authentication) and 1813 (accounting). Combines auth and authorization. Encrypts ONLY the password field — rest of packet is unencrypted. Vendor-neutral. Used for wireless Enterprise auth and VPN.
RADIUS: UDP 1812/1813, password-only encryption, combined auth+authorization, wireless/VPN. TACACS+: TCP 49, full packet encryption, separated AAA, command authorization, network device admin.
